routes.label: Compare bases with a common altitude

question: In \(\triangle ABC\) with right angle at \(C,\) altitude \(CH\) and median \(CM\) trisect the right angle. If the area of \(\triangle CHM\) is \(K,\) then the area of \(\triangle ABC\) is
solution:
Both \(H\) and \(M\) lie on \(AB\), so triangles \(ABC\) and \(CHM\) have the same altitude \(CH\) to their respective bases \(AB\) and \(HM\). Finding the ratio of those bases will therefore give the area ratio.

Because \(ABC\) is right at \(C\) and \(M\) is the midpoint of its hypotenuse, the hypotenuse-median property gives
\[
CM=\frac{AB}{2}.
\]
The two trisecting segments make an angle of \(90^\circ/3=30^\circ\), so \(\angle HCM=30^\circ\). Triangle \(CHM\) is right at \(H\); hence its side opposite \(30^\circ\) is half its hypotenuse:
\[
HM=\frac{CM}{2}=\frac{AB}{4}>0.
\]
This argument does not depend on which trisecting ray is the altitude.

Using the common positive altitude \(CH\),
\[
\frac{\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)}{K}
=\frac{\tfrac12 AB\cdot CH}{\tfrac12 HM\cdot CH}
=\frac{AB}{HM}=4.
\]
Therefore the area of \(ABC\) is \(\boxed{4K}\), choice E.
